name: Shillong
description: Capital city and district headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. Scenic hill station at about 1,496 m with colonial architecture, markets, viewpoints, and base for exploring the region.
facts: Base for trips to Sohra and other attractions

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city, surrounding hills, and Bangladesh plains on clear days. Sacred site for Khasi people with Air Force station nearby.
facts: Highest point in Meghalaya at ~1965 m
Sacred to Khasi deity U Lei Shillong
Requires ID for entry due to radar station

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall in Upper Shillong, originally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Surrounded by lush greenery and ferns, easily accessible and popular for short visits.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city center
Named after a rock that once resembled an elephant

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at 340 m near Sohra (Cherrapunji). Dramatic drop into a turquoise pool from the plateau edge, fed by heavy rainfall, with local legend of Ka Likai.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Sub-divisional town on a plateau at about 1,430 m, historically one of the wettest places on Earth. Gateway to waterfalls, caves, living root bridges, and viewpoints over Bangladesh plains.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village known as Asia's cleanest, with community-led cleanliness, traditional Khasi homes, bamboo skywalk, and nearby living root bridge at Riwai. Near Bangladesh border.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia in 2003
Features living root bridge and skywalk

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi people over centuries. Requires a steep trek of about 3,000-3,500 steps from Tyrna.
facts: Part of UNESCO tentative Living Root Bridges

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint about 25 km from Shillong, meaning 'end of the hills'. Offers panoramic views of deep gorges, rolling hills, and villages, with steep steps to explore.
facts: Khasi name means end of slopes/hills
Popular for photography and short treks

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove near Mawphlang village, protected by Khasi tradition as the abode of a deity. Biodiversity hotspot with old trees, monoliths, and rule against removing anything from the forest.
facts: Protected for centuries by local beliefs
No removal of any plant or object allowed
Site of monoliths and cultural significance

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave near Sohra with stalactites and stalagmites, about 150 m of lit passages. Popular short visit for tourists exploring the wettest region.
facts: Lit show cave suitable for beginners

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters)
description: Segmented waterfall about 315 m high near Mawsmai, cascading in multiple streams over limestone cliffs. Spectacular during monsoon with views toward Bangladesh plains.
facts: Also known as Seven Sisters Falls
